programDesc: A balanced three-day home strength program for a leaner, toned physique. Alternate workout A and workout B across Monday, Wednesday and Friday, continuing the sequence the next week. Train legs, glutes, back, chest, arms and core without focusing on wider shoulders or maximizing glute size. Warm up briefly and perform an easy preparation set before the first heavy movement. Use a comfortable squat, lunge and step-up depth and never force painful joint ranges. Keep about two or three clean repetitions in reserve. Starting weights for new movements are guidelines to check at the first session. FitTimer offers progression after four completed instances of each exercise; accept only if technique and recovery allow. Use consistent band anchor, distance and range to track resistance. Strength training helps preserve muscle during weight loss, but gradual fat loss also requires everyday activity and a suitable calorie deficit. Core-control drills do not promise anatomical changes to spinal curvature. Stop movements causing joint pain.
plans: Supine breathing with legs on bench

Lie on your back with lower legs resting on a stable bench and knees bent. Breathe in gently through your nose, then slowly exhale, allowing lower ribs to settle. Do not force the abdomen inward or press the lower back into the floor.
Avoid breath-holding, shrugging and excessive rib flaring.
Cat–cow
Begin on hands and knees, wrists below shoulders and knees below hips. Slowly round the spine, then return and gently extend it within a comfortable range.
Avoid jerking or forcing the low back into an extreme arch.
Unweighted glute bridge
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart. Lift hips with the glutes until shoulders, hips and knees roughly align, pause briefly and lower slowly. Keep this warm-up easy.
Do not arch the low back or flare ribs to lift higher.
Goblet squat

Stand with feet roughly shoulder-width and toes slightly out. Hold one dumbbell at the chest with both hands. Bend hips and knees to squat as far as comfortably controlled, keeping the whole foot grounded. Let knees track with toes and rise without a low-back arch.
Do not let knees collapse inward. Shorten depth if heels lift or the front of the hip pinches. Knees passing toes are not automatically wrong.
Band row to waist

Secure a long band in front of you around waist height and test the anchor. Sit or stand stable, grasp the ends and draw elbows back near your sides toward the lower ribs. Pause briefly and slowly straighten the arms without rocking.
Do not lean back, shrug or let the band snap forward.
Two-dumbbell Romanian deadlift

Stand hip-width with a dumbbell in each hand. Slightly bend knees and push hips backward, hinging forward while keeping weights close to the legs. Lower until hamstrings stretch with a neutral back, then bring hips forward to stand without leaning back.
Avoid turning this into a squat, rounding the back or forcing a deeper range.
Bench incline push-up

Place hands on a stable bench slightly wider than shoulder-width and step back into a straight-body position. Slowly lower the chest toward the bench with elbows angled backward, then press up without allowing the hips to sag.
Avoid wide elbow flaring, low-back sagging and unstable supports.
Floor push-up

Place hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulders and keep a straight line from head to heels. Slowly lower the chest with elbows angled backward and a little outward, then press up without sagging. Return to an incline if form breaks.
Avoid sagging hips, excessive elbow flaring and bouncing through repetitions.
Weighted bench hip thrust

Rest the lower shoulder blades on a stable bench with feet hip-width. Place a padded weight across the pelvis and secure it with both hands. Lift hips using the glutes until the torso and thighs roughly align, pause and lower slowly with ribs relaxed.
Do not arch the low back to lift higher, use an unstable bench or let the weight roll.
Dead bug

Lie on the back with arms above the chest and hips and knees bent at right angles. Exhaling, slowly reach the right arm behind the head and extend the left leg forward only as far as the pelvis and low back stay controlled. Return and switch sides.
If the low back arches noticeably or hips rock, reduce the leg range. Keep breathing.
Supine breathing with legs on bench

Lie on your back with lower legs resting on a stable bench and knees bent. Breathe in gently through your nose, then slowly exhale, allowing lower ribs to settle. Do not force the abdomen inward or press the lower back into the floor.
Avoid breath-holding, shrugging and excessive rib flaring.
Cat–cow
Begin on hands and knees, wrists below shoulders and knees below hips. Slowly round the spine, then return and gently extend it within a comfortable range.
Avoid jerking or forcing the low back into an extreme arch.
Unweighted glute bridge
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart. Lift hips with the glutes until shoulders, hips and knees roughly align, pause briefly and lower slowly. Keep this warm-up easy.
Do not arch the low back or flare ribs to lift higher.
Weighted step-up

Place the full foot on a stable platform at the height already used comfortably. Step up mainly using the elevated leg instead of pushing off hard with the lower foot. Stand tall without arching, then lower slowly. Complete a set for each leg holding dumbbells at the sides.
Avoid jumping from the lower foot, knee collapse and twisting the pelvis. Reduce the load if balance suffers.
High-anchored band pulldown

Secure a long band high overhead and test the anchor. Sit or kneel facing it with arms raised. Pull elbows down by your sides until hands approach the upper ribs, then slowly reach back overhead, keeping the torso nearly upright.
Avoid leaning far back, jerking the band or shrugging the shoulders.
Stationary dumbbell split squat

Hold one dumbbell in each hand, step back and place feet about hip-width rather than along one tight line. Without moving the feet between repetitions, bend both knees to a comfortable depth and rise through the front leg. Finish one leg then switch.
Avoid a tightrope stance, collapsing the front knee inward or forcing depth through hip pain.
Neutral-grip dumbbell floor press

Sit on the floor with dumbbells near the thighs, carefully lie back and bring weights to the chest. Bend knees, feet flat and palms facing each other. Press above mid-chest, then lower beside the chest until the backs of the upper arms gently touch the floor. Press without bouncing, then roll to the side to sit up safely.
Avoid elbows pointing directly sideways, bouncing off the floor, bent-back wrists or excessive low-back arching.
Bird dog

Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Slowly reach the right arm forward and the left leg backward without twisting the pelvis. Pause for a second, return and switch sides. Do not lift the limbs above the back.
Avoid arching the lower back, rotating the hips or jerking the limbs.
Kneeling side plank

Lie on the side with elbow directly under shoulder and knees bent. Resting on forearm and knees, lift the hips into a line from shoulders through hips to knees. Breathe steadily and avoid sagging, then lower and switch sides.
End the hold if hips sag or the shoulder shrugs. Keep the elbow directly beneath the shoulder.
Straight-leg side plank

Lie on the side with the elbow beneath the shoulder and legs straight. Stack feet or put the top foot slightly ahead for balance. Lift hips into a straight line from head to feet and breathe calmly. Lower slowly and switch sides.
Avoid sagging hips, rolling the chest toward the floor or shrugging the supporting shoulder.
